intended_object: The Smith-normal-form invariant factors d₁ | d₂ | … | dₙ (positive) of the Gram matrix of a nondegenerate integral lattice in a chosen ℤ-basis, i.e. the orders of the cyclic factors of the discriminant group L^♯/L (docstring and module doc).
explanation: The body chooses d from an existence statement giving P, Q ∈ GLₙ(ℤ) and d with all dᵢ > 0, dᵢ ∣ dⱼ for i ≤ j, and P·G·Q = diag d, where G is the Gram matrix of the basis reindexed by Fin (card ι). A positive diagonal with a divisibility chain is unique (`Matrix.smith_normal_form_unique`), so the chosen d is exactly the normalized Smith invariant factors of G. The library also proves that it does not depend on the basis (`gramSmithInvariantFactors_eq`), via the change-of-basis formula Tᵀ G T. The normalization (positive, ascending divisibility) is standard, and the rank-0 case gives the empty family, as it should. Nondegeneracy (det G ≠ 0) is genuinely needed for the factors to be positive. Mathlib has Smith normal form only for submodules over a PID (`Basis.SmithNormalForm`, `Ideal.smithCoeffs`), not invariant factors of a Gram matrix, so there is no more general counterpart and the definition is not too narrow.
